note: Repeat runs of conformance case 155 after the use-after-free fix (f377c73c), to replace a per-format claim that had been read off a single instrumented run. Set `rate-*` is verdict-only; set `lane-*` carried a temporary printf on the post-UpdateTexture readback reporting format and pixel-shader lane, reverted afterwards -- it prints only once a mismatch has already been detected, so it cannot influence the outcome. Every failure is the same four assertions at d3d9_conformance_visual_formats.c:796-799, all four texels or none, and the sampled value is always exactly initPalettizedTexture's identity palette (ff010101,ff020202,ff030303,ff040404 for P8; 80010101,40020202,20030303,10040404 for A8P8) with the source alpha preserved.

summary.conclusion: Nondeterministic; affects BOTH formats and BOTH pixel-shader lanes, P8 more often than A8P8. The earlier 'A8P8 only' reading came from a sample of one and is refuted. Same rate and same signature as visual_mvp_software_vp_policy (~40%, all-four-or-none wrong 2x2 expansion); treat as one defect with two repros.

post_heap_retain.note: Second set, after StagingCopy::destHeap was changed to a retained WMT::Reference<WMT::Heap>. That change hardens a hazard that is not currently firing, so it was expected to leave the rate alone; this set confirms it. Recorded because the first four runs of it all passed, which at the measured rate happens ~9% of the time by chance and would have been easy to publish as a fix.

fix.change: src/d3d9/device_c_draw.cpp -- dxmt9c_device_update_texture no longer routes palettized UpdateTexture through core::Device::updateTexture. That path queued a GPU submitSurfaceCopy of the SOURCE texture's Metal backing, which for P8/A8P8 is a derived A8R8G8B8 expansion through the SOURCE's own palette -- and a SYSTEMMEM staging source is never bound via SetTexture, so its palette is still initPalettizedTexture's identity ramp. The destination was then expanded again with its own palette via a different submission path (Initializer::uploadTextureLevel), so one UpdateTexture issued two conflicting full-subresource writes to the same Metal texture on two submission paths with nothing ordering them. The palettized branch now copies the index shadow and re-expands with the DESTINATION's palette, making the expansion the only writer.

causal_controls.note: Env-gated, same binary, since reverted. Establishes sufficiency rather than inferring it from the fix working.

case_185_visual_mvp_software_vp_policy.note: No change targeted this case; it is the second repro of the same defect.

staged_artifacts.note: Fix is entirely unix-side; d3d9.dll is unchanged from the pre-fix runs above.

fix.unresolved: WHY the identity write won ~45% of the time is not established. Instrumented event streams from passing and failing runs are byte-identical through dxmt9's encode layer, including Metal texture identities, so the winner is settled below it. Bounded: intra-blit-encoder ordering is reliable here (post-fix the initializer still issues three same-subresource writes back-to-back in one encoder and the last wins in 40/40). The unordered relationship is between the chunk command buffer's SurfaceCopy and the initializer's command buffer. The fix removes the race rather than ordering it, so this is a known unknown, not a residual risk on this path.
